journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

guards.title: Clicking the date field still shows the calendar
guards.goal: A pointer user who clicks the departure date sees the month and can pick a day

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component passes the input element as the positionElement to vanilla-calendar-pro, which modifies the input's inline styles (setting left/top) and interferes with keyboard event handling, preventing the Tab key from functioning normally.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the datepicker component to use the parent element of the input as the positionElement for the calendar (when the input is not inline and not in a form-adorn) to prevent direct modification of the input element by vanilla-calendar-pro.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key will move focus from the date field to the next field as expected, because the input element will no longer have its inline styles modified by the calendar and will not interfere with keyboard events.
functional_risks: Calendar may be positioned incorrectly if the parent element lacks appropriate positioning context.
Calendar may appear in an unexpected location for inputs in complex layouts.
Change might affect calendar positioning for inputs that are direct children of body or other unpositioned elements.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab when the date field has focus moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that clicking the date field still shows the calendar.
Verify that pressing Escape when the calendar is shown hides the calendar and moves focus back to the date field (as per regression guard).
Verify that selecting a date from the calendar updates the input value correctly.
Verify that the calendar is positioned near the input field as intended.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's calendar popup does not hide when the input loses focus via keyboard navigation (Tab key), because the dismiss logic only responds to focusin on document and pointerdown, which may not fire in time or may be intercepted by the calendar's own keyboard handling. The calendar remains open and intercepts the Tab key, preventing focus movement.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener on the input element to hide the calendar when the input loses focus, ensuring keyboard navigation works naturally.

plan.root_cause: The vanilla-calendar-pro calendar intercepts the Tab keydown event on the date input when the calendar is open, preventing the default focus movement to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown event listener on the date input that stops immediate propagation and hides the calendar when the Tab key is pressed, allowing the browser's default focus navigation to proceed.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while the date field is focused will move focus to the next field (passengers) as expected, because the calendar will close and not intercept the Tab key.
functional_risks: The calendar may hide unexpectedly if the user presses Tab while the calendar is open but the input is not focused (unlikely because listener is on the input).

The hide() call is asynchronous; however, we call it synchronously and set _isShown to false immediately. The calendar's internal hide might be synchronous, but there is a small risk of race conditions.
The stopImmediatePropagation might prevent other legitimate keydown listeners on the input (e.g., from other components). But the input is a simple date field, unlikely.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab when the date field has focus moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that clicking the date field still shows the calendar.
Verify that pressing Escape when the calendar is shown hides the calendar and moves focus back to the date field (regression guard).
Verify that selecting a date from the calendar updates the input value correctly.
Verify that the calendar is positioned near the input field as intended.
